label: Same reachability profile of specified routes on one carrier
term: same reachability profile of specified routes
definition: For one common carrier D : Type, a SpecifiedRoute D pairs graph : Interpretation linkVocabulary Unit D with route : PhysicalGround.Route D Unit Unit. The structure imposes no link between these components. Its anchor is graph.parameter (). For p : PathFormula linkVocabulary (Unit ⊕ {a : Unit // True}) and x : D, SpecifiedRoute.realizes evaluates p in graph.model, assigning the object variable to x and the sole permitted parameter to that graph's anchor. SameReachProfile s t means exactly that s and t have equal anchors and, for every such formula p and every x on the common carrier, s.realizes p x if and only if t.realizes p x. It compares formula extensions pointwise, not just the extension of anchorReach. The formula language has first-order graph formulas, negation, conjunction and finite reflexive reachability, but no route predicates such as Composite, HasIntellect or ComponentOf. Neither equality of route parameters nor Route.Immaterial is part of SameReachProfile; the independence control asserts Route.Immaterial separately for each route.
note: Analyst stipulation for the comparison used by routeIndependenceControl; attribution deferred. Reuses specification syntax and denotation (7ec17771-8ac2-476b-b674-40ef61a2debc) and restricted path specification (f2fa9b1d-6d34-417b-a734-1fb787badd55). This is a same-carrier comparison, not a cross-domain correspondence or an identification of graph adjacency with causation, composition or bearing. A source for this definition would have to adopt this precise graph/route pairing and formula-agreement criterion. Applying it to an original physical ground still requires the open vocabulary-calibration, admissible-interpretation and occurrence/property-to-bearer bridges; the definition itself supplies none of them.
